quickSummary: During Anaphase, centromeres split simultaneously and sister chromatids are pulled toward opposite poles by Anaphase A and B forces, displaying V, L, J, and I shapes. Telophase reverses prophase by decondensing chromatin and reforming nuclear envelopes. Animal cytokinesis proceeds centripetally (outside-to-inside) via an actin-myosin contractile ring. Plant cytokinesis proceeds centrifugally (inside-to-outside) via Golgi vesicles fusing along the phragmoplast to form the middle lamella. Karyokinesis without cytokinesis generates a syncytium.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.3 Anaphase & Telophase Dynamics
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.3 Anaphase & Telophase Dynamics

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Anaphase splits centromeres; reveals V/L/J/I shapes. Animal cytokinesis = Centripetal (furrow). Plant cytokinesis = Centrifugal (cell plate phragmoplast).

conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Anaphase**: Centromeres split simultaneously; sister chromatids separate into individual daughter chromosomes moving toward opposite poles.
  - **Anaphase A**: Shortening of kinetochore microtubules pulls chromosomes poleward.
  - **Anaphase B**: Elongation of overlapping polar microtubules pushes spindle poles further apart.
  - **Chromosome Shapes**: Centromere leads toward pole with trailing arms: **V-shape** (*Metacentric*), **L-shape** (*Submetacentric*), **J-shape** (*Acrocentric*), **I-shape** (*Telocentric*).
• **Telophase**: Chromosomes decondense into diffuse chromatin; nuclear membranes, nucleoli, and Golgi bodies reassemble around daughter nuclei.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.4 Cytokinesis Mechanisms in Animals vs Plants
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.4 Cytokinesis Mechanisms in Animals vs Plants
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
CYTOKINESIS MECHANISMS
                                      │
         ┌────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                         ▼
  ANIMAL CYTOKINESIS (Cleavage Furrow)                      PLANT CYTOKINESIS (Cell Plate)
  ├── **Centripetal Direction** (Outside ──► Inside)        ├── **Centrifugal Direction** (Inside ──► Outside)
  └── Driven by **Actin-Myosin II Contractile Ring**        └── Driven by **Phragmoplast** & Golgi Vesicles
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Animal Cells (Cleavage Furrow)**: An equatorial **Actin-Myosin II contractile ring** constricts the plasma membrane inward in a **Centripetal (outside-to-inside)** direction.
• **Plant Cells (Cell Plate)**: Rigid cell walls prevent furrowing. Golgi-derived vesicles containing calcium/magnesium pectate align along microtubules forming the **Phragmoplast**, growing in a **Centrifugal (inside-to-outside)** direction to form the **Middle Lamella / Cell Plate**.
• **Syncytium**: Repeated nuclear divisions (karyokinesis) without cytoplasmic cleavage (cytokinesis) produce a multinucleated protoplasmic mass (*e.g., liquid endosperm of coconut, coenocytic fungi*).
